newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania's Nano says he will be next prime minister.
newsitem.headline: Albania's Nano says he will be next prime minister.

text.p: Albania's Socialist party chairman, Fatos Nano, said on Sunday he would be the country's next prime minister after the Socialists were officially declared winners of the troubled country's general election.

Nano will replace fellow Socialist Bashkim Fino, who was appointed interim prime minister in March this year when the government resigned and an early election called to stem the violence that erupted after popular savings schemes collapsed.
"I will be the prime minister," Nano told reporters at a second round of voting held on Sunday to decide a number of outstanding seats.
"The leader of the party will become the leader of the executive. Fino will be (on my) right side."

Nano, a multi-lingual economist, has been prime minister twice -- at the head of Albania's last communist administration in 1991 and after the first multi-party elections won by the Socialists, the heirs to Albania's communists.
But after the Democratic Party of President Sali Berisha won power in 1992, Nano was implicated in an Italian aid scandal and in 1994 was jailed for 12 years.
He was freed and pardoned in March this year and has campaigned to promote a new image for socialism in Albania, Europe's poorest country, that believes in free enterprise and private property.

On Saturday the Socialists were confirmed the winners of the poll by the Central Electoral Commission, securing over 80 of 155 assembly seats in the first vote on June 29, overwhelmingly defeating the Democrats.
Many Albanians blame Berisha for the collapse of the pyramid schemes, in which thousands lost life savings, and for the ensuing violence in which over 1,500 people were killed.
Run-off ballots were being held on Sunday in 34 seats across the country where no candidate had won a clear majority.
This second round would decide whether the Socialists and their leftist allies had the two-thirds majority needed in parliament to make constitutional changes -- and to vote in a new head of state.
Berisha has pledged to stand down as president once a leftist government is appointed. Nano declined to comment on possible candidates for the position.
Nano said he was confident the Socialists and their allies had already secured two-thirds of the assembly.
"The coalition government has got two thirds. There is no doubt about that," said Nano, sporting a beard that would have been forbidden during Albania's 45 years of hardline communism.
"It is very sure now, with this already large mandate, that people voted in this election for a new way of rebuilding a democratic civilization in Albania."
Nano said it was important to act quickly to start rebuilding Albania and the Socialists were seeking legal advice about convening the new parliament within the next two weeks.

The new government has an uphill task to restore order in many areas of southern Albania which remain in the grip of criminal gangs but Nano was confident of success with the country's 3.4 million people wanting an end to the bloodshed.
"The future of Albania will be not only bloody-less but Albanian human blood will give energy to a very specific future for all of us," Nano said.
